introduction: Following the governance shift in 2014, the Government of India launched a series of massive structural welfare programs focusing on financial inclusion, manufacturing, sanitation, and clean energy. This level covers the absolute essentials that form the bedrock of scheme-related factual questions.

core_concepts.title: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)
core_concepts.description:
- Nodal Ministry: Ministry of Finance
- Launch Date: August 28, 2014
- Core Objective: National Mission for Financial Inclusion to ensure access to financial services namely, basic savings & deposit accounts, remittance, credit, insurance, and pension in an affordable manner (Universal banking access).

core_concepts.title: Make in India
core_concepts.description:
- Nodal Ministry: Ministry of Commerce and Industry (Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade - DPIIT)
- Launch Date: September 25, 2014
- Core Objective: To transform India into a global design and manufacturing hub, stimulate foreign direct investment (FDI), and optimize 25 focus sectors.

core_concepts.title: Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM)
core_concepts.description:
- Nodal Ministry: Ministry of Jal Shakti (for SBM-Gramin) & Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (for SBM-Urban)
- Launch Date: October 2, 2014
- Core Objective: To achieve universal sanitation coverage, eliminate open defecation (ODF status), and ensure scientific solid waste management across rural and urban India.

core_concepts.title: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY)
core_concepts.description:
- Nodal Ministry: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
- Launch Date: May 1, 2016 (Launched from Ballia, Uttar Pradesh)
- Core Objective: To safeguard the health of women and children by providing free LPG (Liquefied Petroleum Gas) connections to women from BPL (Below Poverty Line) households, replacing unhealthy conventional cooking fuels.

important_entities.name: The 2014 Institutional Baseline
important_entities.significance: PMJDY, Make in India, and SBM were all launched within a 3-month window in late 2014. In chronological matching questions, remember the sequence: Jan Dhan (August) ➡️ Make in India (September) ➡️ Swachh Bharat (October).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Examiners frequently try to confuse students by listing the Ministry of Health or Ministry of Environment for SBM. Note the strict bifurcation: Rural sanitation is under the **Ministry of Jal Shakti**, while Urban sanitation belongs to the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)**.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Wealthy (Jan Dhan) Makers (Make in India) Clean (Swachh Bharat) the nation.
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Helps lock down the exact chronological sequence of the three cornerstone schemes launched consecutively in Aug, Sept, and Oct of 2014.

exam_strategy_tips: For one-liner factual exams (SSC, State Exams), memorize the specific launch location of PMUY (Ballia, UP). It is frequently tested as a standalone trivia question.
